missed_mechanics: Pac’s bubble top contact only rebounds when Pac is airborne and falling onto the bubble from above; the projectile survives this contact.
The same surviving projectile can then hit Isp and grant FLOAT, so the route shares one shot sequentially rather than allocating or reusing it after consumption.
The partner-assisted jump is the setup for Pac’s required high route; Isp then uses FLOAT to reach the farther duct.
The floor is continuous, the room has no authored hazards/collectibles, and missed shots repeat.
incorrect_inferences: The pass-one uncertainty that a bubble might be consumed by Pac’s first contact was resolved the other way: the special top-bounce leaves that projectile in flight.
changed_judgments: Cooperation and execution rise from 2 to 3 because the legal route requires an assisted Pac launch, a precisely oriented top contact, and Isp’s follow-up FLOAT.
Timing changes from unknown to 3 because the same shot must reach Pac and then Isp in sequence; the automatic 1-second windup/cooldown makes retries possible but does not remove the dependency.
Hazards change from unknown to 0 and recovery from unknown to 1 because there is no lethal hazard and the continuous floor plus repeating shots support a safe retry.
Novelty rises from 2 to 3 because known FLOAT and partner-ride lessons are recombined with a projectile-preserving Pac bounce.
unresolved: No retained ordinary-input route or retry trace was available. Whether two novices discover the special collision angle and sequence, and how often they miss it, remains unknown.

single_operator_note: One operator would need to time Pac’s ride/jump/top contact while also moving Isp ahead to receive the same projectile, then steer Isp during FLOAT. This simultaneous attention demand is separate from the two-human ratings.
